techniques.name: Biquad (RBJ cookbook) as the universal primitive
techniques.what: Every filter below is one Direct-Form-I biquad: y[n]=b0*x + b1*x1 + b2*x2 - a1*y1 - a2*y2. RBJ formulas give LP, high/low-shelf, peaking-EQ, and bandpass/resonator coefficients from (fc, Q, gain). Chain them for the hull transfer function; run them in parallel (summed) for modal banks and cavity resonances.
techniques.fit: Add one `struct Biquad{b0,b1,b2,a1,a2,z1,z2}` with `process(&mut self,x:f32)->f32`. Our synth already emits f32 buffers, so we just fold `.map(|s| chain.process(s))` over the buffer before wrapping it in a rodio `SamplesBuffer`. Zero deps.
techniques.cost: ~5 mults/sample per biquad; a 20-mode bank + 6 cavity peaks is <30 biquads, trivial for one-shots.

techniques.name: Modal synthesis with INHARMONIC plate/bar ratios (the struck-plate upgrade)
techniques.what: Bank of 2-pole resonators, one per mode. Key fix vs a harmonic model: plate partials go as f_mn ∝ m² + (α·n)² (α = Lx/Ly aspect), NOT integer multiples — this is what makes steel sound clangy/metallic instead of pitched. Ideal free-free steel BAR ratios (spall/ringing rod): 1 : 2.76 : 5.40 : 8.93 : 13.3 (from B(1)=1.506,B(2)=2.500,B(k≥3)=k+0.5, squared). Circular membrane (drum/skin thunk): 1 : 1.59 : 2.14 : 2.30 : 2.65 : 2.92. Per-mode resonator from target T60: R = exp(-6.908/(T60_k·fs)), θ=2π·f_k/fs, then y[n]=x[n]+2R·cosθ·y1 − R²·y2. Frequency-dependent damping (higher modes die faster): T60_k = T60_0·(f_0/f_k)^p, p≈0.6–1.0, i.e. loss R_k = b1 + b3·f_k².
techniques.fit: Vec<Biquad> in resonator mode; sum outputs, drive with the excitation buffer, render to f32, hand to a detached Sink exactly like existing one-shot Sfx. Strike position variation via sin(mπx/Lx)·sin(nπy/Ly) per-mode weights, x/y picked from the existing counter-seeded integer hash — no rand.
techniques.cost: Cheap; 12–24 resonators per impact. Baked once into the buffer, not streamed.

techniques.name: Half-sine excitation → hardness/contact-time control
techniques.what: Model the strike force as a half-sine pulse of contact time tc. Its spectrum is ~flat to ~1/(2tc) then rolls off (first null at 1.5/tc — NIST impact-echo result). Harder/faster/stiffer contact ⇒ shorter tc ⇒ brighter (excites high modes) ⇒ 'ping'; softer ⇒ longer tc ⇒ only low modes ⇒ 'thud'. Implement without a literal pulse: multiply each modal gain by a one-pole rolloff E(f_k)=1/(1+(f_k/fc)²), fc=1/(2tc). Map game 'hardness' 0..1 to tc ≈ 2ms (soft, fc≈250Hz) … 0.05ms (steel-on-steel, fc≈10kHz).
techniques.fit: One extra multiply on each modal amplitude at buffer-synth time; 'hardness' becomes a single synth parameter. Contact-time = the knob that turns a hollow bong into a sharp shell-strike crack.

techniques.name: Residual noise transient (Microsoft/Crackdown-II SOTA)
techniques.what: Modal bank alone misses the chaotic attack. Lloyd/Raghuvanshi 'Sound Synthesis for Impact Sounds in Video Games' (I3D 2011) layer a 2–5 ms filtered-noise residual under the modes, shaped by the SAME excitation LP (fc=1/2tc). This is what makes synthetic impacts 'indistinguishable from recordings'.
techniques.fit: Add a 2–5ms burst of hashed white noise through the excitation LP to the front of the impact buffer. We already have the deterministic hash for the noise.

techniques.name: Directional cues without HRTF (constant-power pan + ITD + head-shadow LP)
techniques.what: Three stacked cues that read on headphones AND speakers, for azimuth θ (+=right): (1) Constant-power pan: gL=cos(π/4·(1+p)), gR=sin(π/4·(1+p)), p=sin θ. (2) ITD per-ear delay: Δt = 0.66 ms·sin θ (max human ITD ≈660 µs at ±90°; ≈32 samples @48kHz) — delay the FAR ear; keep ≤0.7ms or it phases. (3) Head-shadow ILD: one-pole LP on the FAR ear only, fc = 2000 + 18000·(1−|sin θ|) Hz (down to ~2kHz at full side) plus far-ear gain ×(1 − 0.3|sin θ|). Weak front/back cue: −3dB HF shelf above 4kHz for sources behind.
techniques.fit: Synth L and R buffers separately: per-ear integer-sample delay offset, per-ear LP biquad, per-ear gain; interleave into a stereo `SamplesBuffer`. rodio plays stereo natively. ITD as an index offset needs no fractional interpolator at these magnitudes.
techniques.cost: Doubles per-impact synth work (2 channels); still nothing for one-shots.

techniques.name: Schroeder/Freeverb reverb tuned to a steel box
techniques.what: 4–8 parallel feedback-comb filters + 2 series allpass. Set comb delays to the box's wall round-trip times (see interior_model) so the coloration IS the cavity. Feedback g = 10^(−3·delay/RT60). Damp each comb's feedback with a one-pole LP (Freeverb 'damp' ≈0.2–0.4) so highs die faster than the low boom.
techniques.fit: Vec<f32> ring buffers; pure integer indexing. Since rodio has no effects bus, either bake the box IR (~0.4s) once and convolve it into each interior one-shot, or run the comb/allpass over the buffer at synth time.
techniques.cost: IR convolution of a 0.4s IR per one-shot is fine; or precompute IR and do FFT convolution if many overlap.

interior_model:
BUTTONED-UP HULL (concrete chain applied to any EXTERIOR airborne event before playback):

Steel transmission loss follows field-incidence mass law TL(f)=20·log10(m·f)−47 dB, m=surface density=7850·thickness. 25mm→m=196 kg/m²: TL≈41dB@125, 47@250, 53@500, 59@1k, 65@2k, 71@4k. 80mm→m=628: add ~10dB. Coincidence dip at fc≈12/thickness_mm kHz (25mm→480Hz, 80mm→150Hz), then TL climbs steeply. Net transfer function = a low-pass shelf: near-flat heavy attenuation at LF, rising ~6dB/octave above ~200Hz. DO NOT apply the literal 40–70dB or the crew hears nothing — games compress. Recipe chain:
1. Broadband gain −18 to −24 dB.
2. Low-pass biquad fc≈600–800 Hz, Q≈0.707 (12 dB/oct) — the dominant 'muffled' cue.
3. Low-shelf +3 to +6 dB below 120 Hz (the boom that penetrates).
4. Cavity resonance peaks (see below), Q 5–10, +3 to +6 dB each — the 'boxy' color.

CAVITY MODES of a ~10 m³ steel box (≈3.0×2.0×1.6 m): f = (c/2)·√((l/Lx)²+(m/Ly)²+(n/Lz)²), c=343. Axial fundamentals: Lx→57 Hz, Ly→86 Hz, Lz→107 Hz; add harmonics 114, 172, 214 Hz. Place 3–5 peaking biquads at 57/86/107/172/214 Hz.

CREW-COMPARTMENT REVERB (Sabine RT60=0.161·V/(S·ᾱ), V≈9.6 m³, S≈28 m²): bare steel ᾱ≈0.03 ⇒ RT60≈1.8s (too ringy/unrealistic); packed with crew+ammo+padding ᾱ≈0.12–0.18 ⇒ RT60≈0.25–0.45 s. USE RT60≈0.30–0.40 s, bright metallic early reflections. Comb delays = wall round-trips: Lz/c=4.7ms, Ly/c=5.8ms, Lx/c=8.7ms, min-dim slap 9.3ms, plus 11/13ms; feedback g=10^(−3·delay/0.35): e.g. 8.7ms→0.842. Two allpass smears at ~1.7ms and ~5ms, g=0.5. Pre-delay ≈0. Flutter between parallel steel walls at 4.7/5.8/8.7 ms is desirable metallic character — keep delays only mildly coprime.

STRUCTURE-BORNE (bypasses airborne TL entirely — dominates what the crew actually hears):
- Engine (Maybach HL230 V12): firing fundamental = rpm/60·6. Idle ~600rpm→60 Hz; ~2000rpm→200 Hz. Synth = sum of sine/saw at fundamental + 6–8 harmonics, amplitude/pitch modulated by rpm, through a LP ~1.5–2 kHz AND the cavity peaks above. Always-on layer (fits the existing looping LayerState pattern).
- Tracks/roadwheels: broadband metallic impact clicks gated at roadwheel-pass frequency (speed-dependent), each click = a short modal 'clank' (bar ratios) through LP ~2 kHz. Louder/brighter than engine on hard turns.
concussion_model:
CONCUSSION / BLAST ON HEARING. Drive everything from one intensity s∈[0,1] (from overpressure or distance): near-miss artillery ≈ 0.3–0.6, close/penetrating hit ≈ 0.8–1.0.

TINNITUS RING: oscillator at f_ring = 4000 Hz for near-miss (the classic 4 kHz acoustic-trauma notch), rising to 6000–7500 Hz for a sharp/penetrating hit. Add organic wobble: 4–6 Hz tremolo ±1 dB + a few-Hz vibrato so it isn't a sterile test tone. Gain envelope: attack 5 ms (near) / 2 ms (hit) to peak level = −(6 + 6·(1−s)) dB; then exponential decay with τ = 1.5 s (near) … 5 s (hit); audible ≈ 3τ.

WORLD DUCK (side-chain the ambience/engine/other sinks): drop to gain 10^(−(6 + 18·s)/20) dB (i.e. −6 dB light, −24 dB at s=1). Recover linear-in-dB over T_rec = 2 + 12·s seconds (≈2–14 s).

'DEAFENED' MUFFLE (master low-pass sweep): fc(t) starts at fc0 = 8000·(1 − 0.9·s) Hz (down to ~800 Hz at s=1) and sweeps back to 18 kHz over T_rec, exponential in log-frequency. This HF-notch reads as 'temporary threshold shift' — TTS is a high-frequency loss, so a LP (not a boom cut) is correct.

PENETRATING-HIT DROPOUT: for s>0.8, a 100–300 ms near-total mute at t=0 ('hearing cuts out'), then the ring fades in and the muffle recovers. This single trick sells a direct hit.

DURATION-BY-OVERPRESSURE SUMMARY: ring τ 1.5→5 s, duck −6→−24 dB, muffle fc0 800→7200 Hz, recovery 2→14 s, all lerped by s. Real TTS recovers over hours; compress to ≤~15 s. Reference: Battlefield/COD concussion (4kHz-ish ring + duck + LP sweep); BF6 added a tinnitus intensity slider — SHIP AN ACCESSIBILITY SLIDER scaling s.

RODIO FIT: rodio has no master DSP insert, so build a tiny custom mixer summing all sources into ONE f32 stream feeding a single OutputStream — then the master LP sweep + duck are one biquad + one gain automated per frame. Ring = a dedicated looping Sink whose set_volume() we automate; duck other sinks via set_volume(). If you skip the custom mixer you get duck-only (no master muffle).
distance_model:
OUTDOOR DISTANCE PROPAGATION.

AIR ABSORPTION (ISO 9613-1/-2, verified table at 10°C / 70% RH — the 'adverse'/reference condition), α in dB/km by octave band: 63→0.1, 125→0.4, 250→1.0, 500→1.9, 1k→3.7, 2k→9.7, 4k→32.8, 8k→117. (At 20°C/70% HF is a bit gentler: 2k≈8.6, 4k≈26, 8k≈88.) Note the exponential HF penalty — this is what turns a distant gun 'crack' into a 'thud'. Per-band loss = α_band·d/1000 dB; add geometric spread 20·log10(d) (−6 dB per distance doubling).

CHEAP SINGLE-BIQUAD APPROXIMATION (don't run 8 bands): replace the band table with one 12 dB/oct low-pass whose cutoff falls with distance (frequency where cumulative absorption ≈6 dB). Precompute & interpolate: 100m→~6kHz, 250m→~3.5kHz, 500m→~2.2kHz, 1000m→~1.5kHz, 2000m→~0.9kHz, 4000m→~0.5kHz. This single LP + a 1/d gain captures the whole 'distant boom' character.

GROUND EFFECT: grazing paths over soft ground (snow/soil) add a mid-frequency interference dip — peaking-EQ −3 to −6 dB, Q≈1, at ~300–500 Hz, plus broadband −3 dB. Snow is very HF-absorptive → push the distance LP one step lower.

URBAN (Stalingrad rubble): hard façades → discrete slapback taps at Δt = 2·building_dist/343 and a short reverb tail; occluding buildings → extra LP + level drop (diffraction shadow).

FLASH-BANG GAP: sound lag = d/343 s (1 km → 2.9 s). Implement literally — on a visible muzzle flash/impact, schedule the audio Sink to spawn at now + d/343 using the existing FX-timer mechanism in Game::update. (Advanced: an incoming supersonic shell's transonic crack arrives BEFORE the muzzle report — optional second event.)

RODIO FIT: apply the distance LP biquad + set Sink volume from the 1/d gain at buffer-synth time; the flash-bang delay is just a deferred Sink spawn (a timer field), which matches the fire-and-forget one-shot Sfx pattern already in audio.rs.
notes:
Sources (verified): ISO 9613-1:1993 absorption formula incl. O2/N2 relaxation freqs & water-vapor term (gorbatschow.github.io/SonarDocs; iso.org/standard/17426). Octave-band α table 10°C/70% confirmed verbatim from a DIN ISO 9613-2 reproduction (help.emd.dk windPRO Appendix A / epa.wa.gov Noise Modelling appendix): 0.1/0.4/1.0/1.9/3.7/9.7/32.8/117 dB/km. Mass-law TL & coincidence (sciencedirect Mass-Law overview; hambricacoustics panel-TL tutorial): +6 dB/oct below fc, +9–18 dB/oct above; fc≈12/thickness_mm kHz. ITD max ≈660 µs @ ±90°, ILD = HF head-shadow LP, ITD useful <1.5 kHz (Wikipedia Interaural time difference; ScienceDirect ITD/ILD; JASA 2019 smallest-perceivable-ITD). Modal ratios & free/clamped plate m²+(αn)², bar B(k) values (Nathan Ho 'Exploring Modal Synthesis'; DLloyd/Raghuvanshi 'Sound Synthesis for Impact Sounds in Video Games', I3D 2011 / Microsoft Research). Half-sine impact spectrum, null at 1.5/tc, hardness→contact-time (NIST Impact-Echo, Carino). Blast TTS/tinnitus 4 kHz notch, hours-to-days recovery, HF-shifting tinnitus (PMC3261792 blast-induced tinnitus in rats; UK MoD 'Blast Injury of the Ear'). Game precedent: Battlefield/COD tinnitus + duck + LP; BF6 tinnitus-intensity slider (ea.com/able) — mirror it as accessibility.

ONE ARCHITECTURAL FLAG: master-bus effects (blast muffle sweep, global duck-with-filter) are impossible through rodio's per-Sink model. Build a small custom mixer — sum every source into one f32 stream, run master biquad(s) + gain, feed a single OutputStream. Everything else (interior coloration, modal impacts, per-ear pan/ITD, distance LP) bakes into the per-one-shot f32 buffer at synth time and needs no bus. All DSP here is plain f32 biquads + integer-indexed ring-buffer delay lines — no external audio crate. Verify via the headless `cargo run -- fire`/`screenshot` loop by dumping synthesized buffers to WAV and inspecting spectra.
